info.title: Orquesta Public API
info.summary: Programmatic access to prompts, logs, projects, agents, users, and the Batuta LLM proxy.
info.description:
The Orquesta Public API exposes read access to your organization's prompts, execution logs,
projects, agents, and users, plus an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions proxy ("Batuta LLM")
that routes across multiple upstream models with smart per-prompt classification.

All endpoints under `/api/v1/*` are stable, versioned, and safe to integrate against. Internal
dashboard endpoints (`/api/projects/[id]/batuta/*`, `/api/agent/*`, `/api/auth/*`, etc.) are
NOT part of this contract and may change without notice.

## Authentication

Pass an API key on every request via either header:

  - `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
  - `X-API-Key: <token>`

Three token prefixes are accepted; each carries different scope semantics:

  | Prefix   | Type              | Scope             | Scopes granted                                          |
  |----------|-------------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
  | `oak_`   | Org API key       | Organization, or a chosen subset of its projects | DB-configured (any of `prompts:read`, `prompts:write`, `logs:read`, ...) |
  | `oclt_`  | CLI token         | Organization      | All four read scopes (synthesized), plus prompt submit    |
  | `oat_`   | Agent token       | Project (single)  | All four read scopes; queries restricted to its project  |

An `oclt_` inherits its creator's access: an org owner or admin reaches every project,
anyone else only the projects they are a member of. Projects outside that set are
reported as not found.

An `oak_` is org-wide unless it was restricted to specific projects when it was created
(or edited afterwards). A restricted key sees only those projects in every listing, and
a request naming any other project is reported as not found — the same answer as a
project that does not exist, so a key cannot enumerate the organization.

Generate keys from the dashboard: https://getorquesta.com/dashboard/settings

## Errors

Non-Batuta endpoints return `{ "error": "human-readable message" }` with status codes
401 (missing/invalid key), 403 (scope/project mismatch), 404 (not found), 500 (internal).

Batuta proxy endpoints (`/chat/completions`, `/models`) return OpenAI-compatible errors:
`{ "error": { "message": "...", "type": "auth_error" | "billing_error" | "routing_error" | "proxy_error" } }`.

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint. Pass any model id from `GET /models` as the
`model` field; pass the synthetic id `batuta-auto` to let Batuta classify the prompt and
route to a tier (fast / balanced / premium) automatically.

### Routing headers (optional)

  - `X-Batuta-Force-Tier: fast | balanced | premium` — bypass the classifier and pin a tier
    for this call. Only meaningful when `model = batuta-auto`.
  - `X-Batuta-Session-ID: <uuid>` — opaque session id. When provided, the proxy attributes
    prior assistant turns in this session to the model that produced them so downstream
    models can calibrate trust on cross-model conversations.

### Routing response headers

  - `X-Batuta-Routed-From: batuta-auto` (when input was routed)
  - `X-Batuta-Routed-To: <upstream-model-id>`
  - `X-Batuta-Tier: fast | balanced | premium`

parameters.name: X-Batuta-Force-Tier
parameters.description: Pin the routing tier. Only honored when `model = batuta-auto`.

parameters.name: X-Batuta-Session-ID
parameters.description: Opaque per-conversation id for cross-model attribution.

200.description: Successful completion (or first SSE chunk if `stream=true`).

X-Batuta-Routed-From.description: Original requested model. Present only when routing happened.

X-Batuta-Routed-To.description: Actual upstream model that produced the completion.

X-Batuta-Tier.description: Tier chosen (or forced) for this call.

429.description: Token quota exceeded for this billing tier.

get.summary: List models available through the Batuta proxy (OpenAI-compatible)

get.description:
Returns prompts ordered by `createdAt` descending. Agent-token (`oat_`) calls are
automatically restricted to the token's project; passing a different `projectId` returns 403.

parameters.name: createdBy
parameters.description: User id of the prompt author

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Only prompts reported by this interactive session (turns an orquesta-cli session self-reports)

post.description:
Queues a prompt on a project's agent. The prompt is created with status `pending`;
the agent picks it up on its next heartbeat (every 15 seconds) and transitions it to
`running` — there is no separate execute call. Poll `GET /api/v1/prompts/{id}` or
`GET /api/v1/logs?promptId=...` for progress.

Requires a token that can be attributed to a user: a CLI token (`oclt_`), or an org
API key (`oak_`) with the `prompts:write` scope. Agent tokens (`oat_`) are rejected —
a token that lives on the machine which would run the prompt cannot enqueue its own work.

A project you cannot reach returns 404, not 403, so ids cannot be probed.

context.description: Arbitrary JSON passed through to the agent.

400.description: Invalid body, or the project has no agent configured.

get.summary: Get a single prompt by id (with context)

patch.description:
Star, tag, assign or re-rate an existing prompt. Requires a CLI token (`oclt_`) or an
org API key (`oak_`) with `prompts:write`; agent tokens are read-only. `assigned_to`
must be a member of the same organization.

400.description: No valid fields, a wrong field type, or an assignee outside the organization.

post.summary: Cancel a pending or running prompt
post.description:
Tells the project's agent to stop the prompt and marks it `failed` with error
`Cancelled by user`. A prompt that already finished keeps its outcome and the call
returns `cancelled: false` with its current status. Requires a CLI token (`oclt_`) or an
org API key with `prompts:write`; agent tokens are rejected.

get.summary: List execution logs by prompt or project
get.description:
Either `promptId` or `projectId` is required. When `promptId` is set the logs are ordered
ascending by `sequence`; when `projectId` is set they are ordered descending by `timestamp`.

parameters.name: afterSequence
parameters.description: With `promptId` only: return logs whose `sequence` is greater than this, for incremental polling.

get.description: For agent tokens (`oat_`), returns only the token's project.

get.summary: List registered agents and their online status

get.description:
Org-scoped tokens (`oak_`, `oclt_`) return organization members. Agent tokens (`oat_`)
return members of the token's project. Useful for resolving `createdBy` ids to email/name.

Forbidden.description: Insufficient scope, revoked token, or project-scope mismatch.

NotFound.description: Resource not found (or invisible to your scope).

BatutaAuthError.description: Missing or invalid Batuta proxy token.

BatutaBillingError.description: Batuta LLM access denied (no subscription, suspended, etc.).

BatutaInvalidRequest.description: Malformed request body (missing model, messages, etc.).

BatutaProxyError.description: Internal proxy error or upstream failure.

model.description:
Any id returned by `GET /models`, or the synthetic `batuta-auto` to enable
classifier-driven routing.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the function arguments

model.description: The upstream model that actually generated the completion

sessionId.description: Interactive session that reported this prompt (context.sessionId)

context.description: Arbitrary context attached at creation time

result.description: The agent's final deliverable (JSON: usually a summary/text); null until the prompt completes

message.description: Truncated at 10K chars. Full content is in `details`.

iconUrl.description: Project icon: the published site's favicon, else the GitHub repo owner's avatar. Null when the project has neither.

agentInfo.description: Hostname, version, platform reported by the agent

role.description: Org role for org-scoped tokens, project role for agent tokens
